texts.preamble: State Of Maharashtra vs Pravin Mishrilal Diwvedi And 2 Others on 11 June, 2018 Author: Swapna Joshi Bench: Swapna Joshi Judgment apeal127.06 1 In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay, Nagpur Bench, Nagpur Criminal Appeal No.127 Of 2006 State of Maharashtra at the instance of Shri S.V. Mulay, Food Inspector, Food and Drug Administration, Bajaj Nagar, Amravati. ..... Appellant.
texts.facts: The prosecution case in a nut shell can be summarized as under: Complainant is a Food Inspector. He was discharging his duties with the Office of the Joint Commissioner, Food and Drug Administration, Amravati over the local area of the Amravati District. Respondent/accused No.1 claims to be a vendor while respondent/accused No.2 a proprietor of M/s. Diwvedi Bandhu Naswale situated at the main road of Dhamangaon (Rly.), District Amravati. It is the case of the prosecution that 10.3.1997, at about 14:30 hours, when the complainant along with one independent witness viz. Ravindra Nilkanthrao Pimpale (PW2) visited the said shop, the complainant and PW2 found respondent/accused No.1 dealing with business in his shop. On disclosing their identity, the complainant inspected the said shop and took samples of food articles, kept there for sale, for testing and analyzing under the provisions of the said Act. The complainant found cloves, Manikchand Gutkha, and Vansh Gutkha in the said shop. The complainant purchased those .....3/- Judgment apeal127.06 16 articles. The complainant complied with the due procedure and prepared samples of those food articles in order to get it tested and analyzed as per the provisions of the said Act. Accordingly, one sealed sample part of Vansh Gutkha was sent to the Public Analyst at Pune on 11.3.1997, after following the due procedure. In due course, the complainant received the Public Analyst report (Exhibit 29) which disclosed the sample of Vansh Gutkha containing Magnesium Carbonate to the extent of 1.01% and the same was not exhibiting batch number and manufacturing date on its label which contravened the provisions of Rule 32(e) and (f) and also Rule 62 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (for the sake of brevity referred to as the "the said Rules"). The complainant then lodged his complaint against the accused persons. The charge was framed by learned Judicial Magistrate First Class and he proceeded with the Trial against the accused persons. 3. Heard learned Additional Public Prosecutor Shri Amit Chutke for the appellant/State and learned counsel Shri Alok Daga for the respondents/accused. He submitted that the sample, weighing about more than 250 grams, was taken charge from the accused and was sent to the Public Analyst. According to .....4/- State Of Maharashtra vs Pravin Mishrilal Diwvedi And 2 Others on 11 June, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101842895/ 2 Judgment apeal127.06 16 him, provisions under Rule 22 of the said Rules are followed by the prosecution. 4. Per contra, learned counsel Shri Alok Daga for the respondents/accused submitted that Public Analyst Report makes it clear that it has received the sample weighing 125 grams. In view thereof, learned Judicial Magistrate First Class has rightly considered the said aspect and has acquitted the accused as the provisions under Rule 22 of the said Rules were not followed by the investigating agency. The testimony of PW1 complainant shows that on 10.3.1997 at about 2:30 p.m., he along with Ravindra Nilkanthrao Pimpale (PW2) visited shop of the accused named as M/s. Diwvedi Bandhu Naswale situated at the main road of Dhamangaon (Rly.), District Amravati for the purpose of inspection. PW1 Complainant found that accused No.1 was incharge of the said shop. He disclosed them his identity as well as identity of the pancha and purpose of visiting their shop. PW1 complainant found loose cloves, Vansh Gutkha, and Manikchand Gutkha in their shop which were kept for sale. He purchased 6 packets of Vansh Gutkha weighing about 750 grams from the said shop for the purpose of its inspection and analysis by making payment of the said Gutkha. He .....5/- Judgment apeal127.06 16 obtained a bill (Exhibit 17) from respondent/accused No.1 in that regard. He recorded an inspection note and delivered a copy of the same (Exhibit 18) to respondent/accused No.1. PW1 issued accused No.1 intimation in Form No.6 (Exhibit 19) about taking samples for analysis and obtained his acknowledgement. PW1 enquired accused No.1 as to from where those articles came to be purchased and accordingly he issued Notice (Exhibit 20) under Section 14-A of the said Act. PW1 prepared 3 samples of the said Gutkha each containing two packets. He pasted paper slips bearing code number AMT/18/ND and serial No.438 signed by the Local Health Authority i.e. the Assistant Commissioner Food and Drug Administration, Amravati. PW1 then recorded a detailed panchanama (Exhibit 21). 6. The testimony of PW1 indicates that on 11.3.1997, he sent sealed sample to the Public Analyst, State Health Loboratory at Pune along with requisite Form No.7 (Exhibit 22). He also sent a copy of Form No.7 along with a specimen impression to the said Public Analyst separately. He received postal acknowledgement in that regard. He delivered the remaining 2 sample parts along with two copies of Form No.7 in an envelope and also sealed two specimen sealed impression in another envelope and delivered the same to the Assistant Commissioner and Local Health Authority, Amravati by issuing forwarding letter. PW1 received the Public Analyst Report with regard to the said samples through the Local .....6/- Judgment apeal127.06 16 Health Authority (Exhibit 29). PW1 issued a letter to accused No.1 requiring him to submit the requisite particulars of that establishment and the name of the seller from whom such articles of food namely Vansh Gutkha was purchased. The reply (Exhibit State Of Maharashtra vs Pravin Mishrilal Diwvedi And 2 Others on 11 June, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101842895/ 3 31) was received by PW1 from accused No.1. On 25.11.1997, PW1 sought consent from the consenting authority for prosecuting the accused persons under the said Act. He obtained the consent accordingly and, thereafter, the present complaint was lodged. 7. In the cross-examination, PW1 fairly stated that each packet of Vansh Gutkha was containing 100 pouches meaning thereby that each packet of Vansh Gutkha was containing 100 pouches i.e. each pouch of 1.25 grams i.e. total 125 grams. PW1, however, denied that he had sent only 125 grams for the food articles of Vansh Gutkha. He further stated that minimum quantity of 200 grams is to be sent to the Public Analyst towards the sample. 8. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor Shri Amit Chutke for the appellant/State vehemently argued that samples of 125 grams were wrongly mentioned in the Public Analyst Report.
texts.arguments: Learned Additional Public Prosecutor Shri Amit Chutke for the appellant/State vehemently argued that learned Judicial Magistrate First Class has not considered evidence led by the prosecution in its right perspective and has acquitted the accused erroneously. In this context, Rule 22 of the said Rules contemplates as under: "Rule 22 : Quantity of sample to be sent to the Public Analyst : The quantity of sample of food to be sent to the Public Analyst/Director for analysis shall be as specified in the table below: Article of Food Approximate quantity t be supplied 1. 9. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor Shri Amit Chutke for the appellant/State does not dispute that as per the old provisions prior to the amendment dated 27.4.2010, the permissible amount was 200 grams.

Learned Additional Public Prosecutor Shri Amit Chutke for the appellant/State does not dispute that as per the old provisions prior to the amendment dated 27.4.2010, the permissible amount was 200 grams.
